sources.title: Arch540_2026 B_testfit PROMPTS.md
sources.extract: Core prompt: lay out buildings on a site for maximum floor area within the planning rules, then draw the plan. Variants add rule-checking script, skill, reviewer, hook (step 5 tries to write a developer scheme unchanged), and with/without-skill comparison.

sources.title: Arch540_2026 B_testfit rules.md
sources.extract: Five rules: 3 m setback; sun gap of at least 0.7 x height of the southern building where east-west extents overlap; 12 m minimum spacing; 40 m maximum height with storey ranges per type; at least 25% of lot unbuilt.

sources.title: Arch540_2026 B_testfit check.py
sources.extract: Shapely-based checker: reads layout JSON and lot polygon, tests R1-R5, prints PASS/FAIL per rule with offending buildings, total GFA and open-space percent; exit codes 0/1/2. Limits: simplified sun-gap test, axis-aligned rectangles, hard-coded thresholds, GFA = footprint x storeys with no core/efficiency deduction.

sources.title: Arch540_2026 B_testfit brief.md
sources.extract: 2D residential test-fit; tower 18x18 m 8-12 storeys, slab 40x12 m 4-8 storeys, short 24x12 m 4-8 storeys; storey height 3.2 m; deliverables layout.json, plan.png and a final message naming the binding rule.

sources.title: Arch540_2026 agents_notes.html (session 4 notes, demos B, C, D)
sources.extract: B_testfit: lot 5,276 m2 (about 90 x 70 m, street south); B1 same prompt gave 16,272 / 13,968 / 15,552 m2; B4 reviewer APPROVE (R1-R5 PASS, both runs); B5 hook gate.py blocked a layout (R2 FAIL, gap 12.0 m, needs 26.9 m), hook never fired in 7 normal runs, and a B5 hook watching the file tool missed the command line; B6 skill changed method (scheme gallery drawn 3 of 3 vs 0 of 3) not floor area. C_design_space: 80 x 60 m Vancouver housing lot (lat 49.25 N), goals GFA, winter sun (average direct-sun hours on open ground, 21 Dec 9:00-15:00, max 6.0) and shape factor; C0 grid search 7,308 combos, 3,680 valid, 8 on the front, all bars; C2 no scorer 50 of 75 valid vs scorer 61 of 75; C3 one run imported the scoring functions directly so evaluations were never counted; C5 six helpers, 329 evaluations, main context near 50k tokens; C6 impossible target, agent stopped after 5 (no hook) or 7 (hook) evaluations. D_team: 100 x 70 m corner block, FSR 2.8, 220-280 homes; hidden contradiction (CEO asks >=250 homes, FSR allows about 239) caught by the constraints helper in 3 of 3 runs; three runs gave three different schemes (237, 222, 226 homes); D3 without the constraints helper a designer estimated about 255 homes, the tool measured 223. Closing lessons: checks in code hold where requests do not; a guard covers only the path it watches; measure rather than estimate; run several times. (An earlier packet text attributed 255 vs 223 to B and the import bypass to B; both claims are corrected here.)

flags.claim: Ladybug licence: 'copyleft either way', so the difference between AGPL and GPL does not matter
flags.detail: Why false: the ladybug core LICENSE (S61) is GNU Affero GPL v3, as are ladybug-grasshopper and honeybee-radiance; Butterfly is GPL-3.0+. AGPL section 13 adds a network-interaction duty that GPL v3 lacks: if you modify the Program, your modified version must offer its source to users interacting with it remotely. For a web platform that wraps or modifies ladybug/honeybee on a server, that duty may attach to the service; whether calling the libraries unmodified, or as a separate process, triggers it is a legal question not settled here.
flags.correction: Record the core libraries as AGPL-3.0. Decision for the DATA packet (not legal advice): either run ladybug/honeybee client-side or in a separately licensed service, or license the platform (or that service) so its source can be offered to users. Hosting any modified Ladybug code means publishing it.

case_studies.what_it_does: Course demo: an agent lays out towers, slabs and short slabs on a 5,276 m2 six-sided lot (about 90 x 70 m, street south) to maximise floor area, checked by a Shapely script against five rules (3 m setback, sun gap 0.7 x southern height, 12 m spacing, 40 m height, 25% open space), with a skill, a reviewer sub-agent and a hook that blocks failing layouts.
case_studies.how_used: Install requirements, copy complete/ (or a steps/ folder) to a new directory, run claude, and paste the prompt from PROMPTS.md. CLAUDE.md caps revisions at six then ends UNRESOLVED.
case_studies.strengths: Demonstrates the validation pattern the course wants: results come from a checker script, a hook enforces it, a reviewer confirms. Evidence in the notes: B1 same prompt gave 16,272 / 13,968 / 15,552 m2; B4 reviewer APPROVE; B5 hook blocked a layout (R2 gap 12.0 m, needs 26.9 m) and never fired in seven normal runs; B6 the skill changed the method (scheme gallery 3 of 3 vs 0 of 3), not the floor area.
case_studies.stops_at: 2D residential toy: 40 m height cap vs 244-305 m VTC towers, three fixed rectangular types, axis-aligned footprints, simplified sun-gap rule instead of a real shadow test, hard-coded thresholds, no cores or efficiency, no VTC site or policy. The B5 hook watched the file tool but not the command line. No licence stated, so reuse terms are unclear.
case_studies.license_cost: Free to clone; no licence declared; running agent demos consumes Claude plan allowance (README warns about long runs).
case_studies.ai_opportunity: Agent loop plus code checker plus hook plus reviewer is a template for evaluation modules: the LLM proposes, the script measures, the gate refuses failures.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: The choice of which rules matter; the checker's own correctness (notes say to test it by hand); a guard covers only the path it watches.

case_studies.tool: GenEnv/Arch540_2026 demo C_design_space (Vancouver winter-sun trade-off front)
case_studies.what_it_does: Course demo on an 80 x 60 m Vancouver housing lot (latitude 49.25 N, street south): massings of boxes (3.2 m storeys, 45 m max, 3 m setback, 6 m spacing) are scored on three conflicting goals, GFA, average winter-sun hours on open ground (21 Dec, 9:00-15:00, 15 m ring, max 6.0 h) and shape factor; the 'front' is the set of designs no other design beats on all three goals.
case_studies.how_used: Copy complete/ or a steps/ folder, run claude, paste a PROMPTS.md variant (one round vs up to six rounds, scorer vs guessing, limit in prompt vs code, skill, family-explorer helpers, impossible target with or without a hook).
case_studies.strengths: Closest existing pattern to a CLIM and PROG trade-off module: grid search gave 7,308 combinations, 3,680 valid, 8 on the front (all bars); several rounds grew the front; with a scorer 61 of 75 designs were valid vs 50 of 75 when the agent guessed, and the guessed best family (courtyard) was wrong; a strategy-library skill surfaced towers, north-high-south-low and terraced forms; six helpers ran 329 evaluations with the main context near 50k tokens; an impossible target ended in a stop after 5 (no hook) or 7 (hook) evaluations without tampering.
case_studies.stops_at: Housing-scale (45 m) and box-only massing; winter-sun metric is an average over open ground, not shadow on a plaza or transit station; no cores, no wind, no view cones. One run imported the scoring functions directly, so the evaluation counter never saw those calls; the complete project's reported counts (180) do not add up to its 300 budget, so reporting is incomplete. No licence stated.

as_is_workflow.step: 0. Register, plan the 40 days, read the brief
as_is_workflow.who: All 2-4 members; one person owns the checklist and the calendar
as_is_workflow.software: PDF reader, shared drive, chat, spreadsheet or whiteboard, calendar; Buildner account
as_is_workflow.input: VTC brief PDF, site plans and 3D model (download buttons on the competition page; links not retrievable by script), the two policy links named in the brief
as_is_workflow.output: Requirements checklist (deliverables, 9.0 FSR non-residential minimum, jury weights 40/30/20/10, deadlines); role split; back-plan. Illustrative back-plan (team assumption, editable): massing frozen about 9 Nov; studies done about 16 Nov; plans and sections about 21 Nov; board drafts about 25 Nov; upload dry-run about 28 Nov.
as_is_workflow.pain_points: As of 21 Oct 2026: registration closes in 8 days (29 Oct), Q&A closes in 13 days (3 Nov, no later questions answered), submission in 40 days (30 Nov 23:59 London = 15:59 Pacific, derived), course working core in 23 days (13 Nov). Ambiguities (FSR basis, view-cone applicability, georeference of the hypothetical site) must be found in week one or they cannot be asked. Obligations are scattered across the brief and two policy documents; vancouver.ca policy PDFs returned HTTP 403 to scripts, so a person must open them in a browser. Fee EUR 140 / EUR 120 plus 4.5% VAT, instalment option mentioned. Time share: unmeasured (team assumption).
as_is_workflow.handover: Reading notes to everyone else; usually a chat message or a doc nobody updates
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Extracting dates, numbers and deliverables, and checking the brief for contradictions (the demo D constraints-helper pattern), is automatable. Interpreting 'City in Nature', reconciliation and which guidelines to justify breaching is human judgment.

as_is_workflow.step: 0b. Cultural, geographic and precedent research and narrative
as_is_workflow.who: All members read; 1-2 lead the narrative; no tool substitutes for engagement
as_is_workflow.software: Library and web sources, reading notes, shared document, image collection
as_is_workflow.input: Brief statement that the site is on the unceded territories of the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations; 'City in Nature'; precedent towers and public spaces; Nation- and City-published material (none opened in this packet)
as_is_workflow.output: Written cultural and environmental narrative with cited sources; precedent list; design principles that feed massing, ground level and boards
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Carries 30% of jury weight yet is easily compressed into a paragraph at the end (team assumption); risk of generic or placeless motifs, which the brief warns against; sources must be cited and the boards carry no identifying information. Time share: unmeasured (team assumption).
as_is_workflow.handover: Narrative to board designers late; principles often do not reach massing or ground-level decisions
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Retrieval, summarising and citation bookkeeping of published documents can be assisted. Interpreting Indigenous perspectives, deciding what to represent and how, and any engagement must not be delegated to a tool; it stays with the team, working from sources by the Nations and the City.

as_is_workflow.software: Rhino (or SketchUp), imported OBJ/IFC/3DM, maybe Speckle; City of Vancouver open data for context
as_is_workflow.input: Provided site plan and 3D model; context towers, approved future towers; north arrow rotated from the street grid; City open data (building footprints 1999/2009/2015, zoning districts, building lines found in a title search; no 3D massing dataset appeared, other titles not searched; licences not checked)
as_is_workflow.output: Georeferenced site and context model, true-north vector, block area (79.2 x 144.8 m = 11,468 m2)
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Orientation error is the costly one: the plan's north arrow is rotated from the street grid, so a wrong angle corrupts every later sun and shadow result. Units come in ft and m (260 x 475 ft = 79.2 x 144.8 m). Imports lose layers or tags (team assumption). Time share unmeasured.
as_is_workflow.handover: Model file passed by drive or email; versions drift; no program tags yet; Speckle Explore keeps only 30 days of versions
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Import, unit conversion, area and orientation checks are automatable. Deciding which context matters is judgment.

as_is_workflow.who: One designer with the modeller; checked by the whole team
as_is_workflow.software: Rhino with imported view-cone polygons (City GeoJSON export), sketching, photo montage
as_is_workflow.input: City open-data 'View cones' (24 protected-view polygons, four of them Queen Elizabeth Park views 3.2.1-3.2.4; Open Government Licence - Vancouver; updated 19 Oct 2026); View Protection Guidelines and Higher Buildings Policy (not opened: HTTP 403); the competition page's 'Queen Elizabeth View Tower Heights' reference photo; brief requirement for a skyline view from Queen Elizabeth Park
as_is_workflow.output: Permissible-height envelope per view cone (once heights are read from the policy), skyline sketch, list of any intended breach with justification
as_is_workflow.pain_points: UNVERIFIED: the dataset says building height is limited inside these views but carries no height field, and the policy PDFs could not be opened, so how heights are set, whether the hypothetical block lies in a cone and which document now governs is unknown. Checked late, a 244-305 m massing may have to be reworked (team assumption). The brief's remark that justified breaches may be rewarded makes the check a judgment, not only a gate.
as_is_workflow.handover: Envelope from views person to massing designers; skyline view to rendering step 7
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Clipping a massing against view-cone volumes is automatable once the height rule is read from the policy. Choosing to breach, and the skyline composition, are judgment.

as_is_workflow.software: Rhino/Grasshopper, SketchUp, sketch paper; sometimes Forma or TestFit if licensed
as_is_workflow.input: Site model, view envelope, brief heights (244-305 m), required mix, hand sketches
as_is_workflow.output: 2-5 massing models; each tagged by use if time allows (becomes Layer 0)
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Options compared by eye; every change means recomputing areas by hand; option count limited by modelling time. Time share: unmeasured, believed largest (team assumption).
as_is_workflow.handover: Models to the spreadsheet person and to the environmental analyst, usually as screenshots or a copied file
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Generating variants and measuring them is automatable (demo C pattern: scorer in code, front in a file). Form, skyline silhouette, expression and the public-uses-through-the-tower idea are judgment.

as_is_workflow.who: One person (often the least modelling-heavy member)
as_is_workflow.input: Floor areas read off the models; use mix; efficiency and core assumptions
as_is_workflow.output: GFA by use, non-residential FSR (brief minimum 9.0), area schedule for the boards
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Manual copy from model to sheet drifts out of date after each massing change. Derived check, assuming the full block as FSR basis (unconfirmed): 11,468 m2 x 9.0 = about 103,200 m2 of non-residential floor area. Derived relationship (editable placeholders, not sourced): office floors N = 103,200 / floor plate; plate 1,500 m2 gives about 69 floors, 2,000 gives about 52, 2,500 gives about 41; at an assumed 4.0 m floor-to-floor that is about 276, 208 and 165 m, so a small plate could use up most of a 244-305 m height and leave little for residential or hotel unless podium floors carry area. Efficiency ratios are usually unsourced team assumptions.
as_is_workflow.handover: Spreadsheet numbers to the board designer; numbers on boards later disagree with the model
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Area take-off, FSR arithmetic, the floors-versus-height calculation and consistency checks are automatable. Choosing the mix, efficiencies and what counts as high-employment use is judgment.

as_is_workflow.software: SketchUp shadows or Rhino sun, Ladybug/Grasshopper, optionally Infrared.city or SimScale; CFD rarely
as_is_workflow.input: Massing model, context, weather/EPW or sun-angle settings, true north
as_is_workflow.output: Shadow images, sun-hour maps, a qualitative or surrogate wind note
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Run once on the final option rather than to compare options; results are pictures without a pass/fail criterion or source; wind is the study most likely to be skipped or reduced to a statement (team assumption); tool access and learning curve (Rhino USD 195 student; Infrared free tokens expire 42 days after sign-up, about 2 Dec if activated 21 Oct; run wind by mid-November, team assumption).
as_is_workflow.handover: Images to boards; findings rarely feed back into massing
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Sun hours, shadow areas and surrogate wind maps are automatable. Selecting the criterion, the day/season and deciding whether a result is acceptable is judgment.

as_is_workflow.who: The environment person plus one designer
as_is_workflow.software: Ladybug/Honeybee, spreadsheet, EC3 (free), possibly Pollination trial; cove analysis.tool is not available to students
as_is_workflow.input: Massing, envelope assumptions (glazing ratio, systems), weather file, material quantities
as_is_workflow.output: Sustainability diagram or short study for the boards (brief lists sustainability studies among recommended deliverables); embodied-carbon estimate
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Benchmarks and efficiency targets are usually unsourced; energy models need envelope and systems assumptions that students invent (team assumption); often reduced to a diagram late in the schedule. Time share unmeasured.
as_is_workflow.handover: Numbers and diagrams to boards; rarely fed back into facade or massing
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Weather processing, solar radiation, simple energy runs and EPD look-ups are automatable. Choosing strategy, targets and trade-offs against daylight and cost is judgment.

as_is_workflow.who: Designer; no engineer on most student teams
as_is_workflow.software: Hand sketches, Illustrator or CAD, rules of thumb
as_is_workflow.input: Massing, height, programme, lift and stair rules of thumb
as_is_workflow.output: Structural strategy diagram, core layout, typical plan cores
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Core and structure sizes are rule-of-thumb and unsourced; core area in the spreadsheet and in plans disagree; structure rarely tested against massing changes (team assumption).
as_is_workflow.handover: Core areas back to the spreadsheet by hand
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Preliminary sizing from stated rules can be automated if the rules are sourced. The structural concept and its architectural expression are judgment.

as_is_workflow.step: 6. Ground level, transit, servicing and public realm
as_is_workflow.input: Site edges (arterial, retail high street, lanes, mid-block connections), below-grade secondary transit entrance requirement, loading and parking needs
as_is_workflow.output: Ground-floor plan, site plan, below-grade connection, servicing diagram
as_is_workflow.pain_points: This is where human-scale experience (40% of jury weight) is decided yet it is often drawn last (team assumption); loading, parking and transit link are coordinated by eye.
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Clearances, loading counts and path lengths can be checked automatically. Public-space quality, entrances and cultural expression are mostly judgment.

as_is_workflow.software: Rhino/CAD (Make2D or equivalent), Illustrator or AutoCAD, Revit or Archicad if used
as_is_workflow.input: Frozen massing, programme, cores and structure, ground-level design
as_is_workflow.output: Site plan, ground floor plan, typical lower, mid and upper plans, at least two sections (brief's recommended deliverables)
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Plans are redrawn after every massing or core change; cut positions chosen late; core and area labels disagree with the spreadsheet (team assumption); line weights and scale inconsistencies across boards. Time share unmeasured.
as_is_workflow.handover: Drawings to board designers as PDFs or Illustrator files, often in mixed formats
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Plan and section extraction from the model and area labelling are automatable. Which cuts to show, drawing conventions and spatial quality are judgment.

as_is_workflow.software: Enscape, Twinmotion, Lumion, V-Ray or similar; Photoshop; possibly AI image tools
as_is_workflow.input: Final model, camera positions (skyline from Queen Elizabeth Park, mid-city, at least four ground-level perspectives)
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Render time and re-rendering after model changes; camera placement for the skyline view; the competition page says AI-generated images may carry ownership and licensing restrictions and are not advised as sole original work.
as_is_workflow.handover: Images to the board layout; file size to be kept for the 10 MB board limit
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Batch rendering and camera setup from coordinates are automatable. Composition, story and drawing choices are judgment.

as_is_workflow.software: Word processor or shared document; policy PDFs opened by hand
as_is_workflow.input: Higher Buildings Policy (1997) and the Higher Buildings Policy Review named in the brief; the scheme's actual heights, FSR and view-cone position; the brief's statement that its documents are academic, not legal
as_is_workflow.output: Written policy reflection for the boards, listing where the scheme follows, tests or breaches guidelines, with justification
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Policy PDFs are hard for a script to reach (HTTP 403) so clauses are quoted second-hand; written last, so justifications are thin (team assumption); the jury may reward justified breaches, so the argument matters more than compliance.
as_is_workflow.handover: Text to board designers; figures must match the spreadsheet
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Clause retrieval with citation and listing which numeric thresholds the scheme exceeds are automatable. Deciding which guideline to breach and why is judgment.

as_is_workflow.software: InDesign, Illustrator, Affinity, Figma or Canva
as_is_workflow.input: Spreadsheet figures, plans, sections, diagrams, renderings, policy reflection text
as_is_workflow.output: Four A2 landscape boards, each at most 10 MB, in English, with no identifying information
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Last-week crunch; layouts rebuilt when options change; numbers on boards drift from the model; identifying metadata or file names can break anonymity (team assumption).
as_is_workflow.handover: Everything converges here; inputs arrive late and in mixed formats
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Number synchronisation, file-size and metadata checks are automatable. Narrative, hierarchy and what to emphasise are judgment.

as_is_workflow.software: Buildner account, unique identification code, PDF export
as_is_workflow.input: Final boards, team member details (editable until the deadline)
as_is_workflow.output: Uploaded entry before 30 Nov 2026 23:59 London time (15:59 Pacific, derived)
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Time-zone confusion, upload failure and size limit at the last minute; fee EUR 140 / EUR 120 plus VAT paid at registration.
as_is_workflow.automatable_or_judgment: Pre-flight checks (size, language, metadata, dimensions) are automatable. The decision to submit is the team's.

notes:
Method: every claim is from a page opened on 21 Oct 2026 (round 0 or r1) unless labelled UNVERIFIED or 'general knowledge'. Prices are as shown on vendor pages that day, in the vendor's currency, and may change. WebSearch was exhausted in r1, so no targeted searches for education offers could run; negative results mean 'not found on the pages opened'. Page text came through a summarising fetch tool; one disagreement with the critique (Infrared tier label) is logged UNRESOLVED rather than silently changed.

Key facts for the team (21 Oct 2026): registration closes 29 Oct, Q&A 3 Nov, submission 30 Nov 23:59 London (40 days from today); teams up to 4. What a student team can get before 30 Nov: Rhino USD 195 student (or a UBC lab licence, ask); Ladybug Tools free; Speckle Explore free (3 users incl. externals, 100 versions, 30-day history) plus a free academic workspace by email application (terms unknown); Giraffe free for students (vendor statement, Vancouver data unverified); Infrared free 900 tokens (expire 42 days after sign-up); Finch and Snaptrude free single-user tiers; SimScale Community free; EC3 free; ShapeDiver 14-day trial or academic programme. Not available to students: cove analysis.tool (academic access ended 31 Dec 2025). Unknown: Autodesk Forma, TestFit (class route), Hypar, Archistar, UpCodes.

Design lessons for the tool: (1) none of the commercial tools expose sourced thresholds, so they are benchmarks, not dependencies; (2) open, scriptable options are Ladybug Tools (AGPL-3.0 for ladybug, ladybug-grasshopper, honeybee-radiance; GPL-3.0+ for Butterfly), Speckle (Apache-2.0) and Hypar Elements/HyparSpace (MIT); the platform licence and deployment boundary are handed to the DATA packet because AGPL section 13 attaches to modified versions offered over a network; (3) the course demos give three module patterns: B (checker script + hook + reviewer), C (scorer, front file, rounds, spending cap in code, per-family helpers) and D (constraints reader that flags contradictions before design, analyst that reports only measured numbers); each also shows a guard covers only the path it watches; (4) AI reduces effort on take-off, scripting, option sweeps, retrieval and contradiction checks, but not on choosing criteria, interpreting 'City in Nature' and reconciliation, deciding which guideline to breach, or any engagement with the Nations; (5) the as-is workflow now includes the steps critics found missing (protected views, cultural research, sustainability, plans and sections, policy reflection). Vancouver's open-data view cones are a verified starting point, but heights and the governing document must be read by a person from the City policy PDFs, which returned HTTP 403. The competition page advises caution with AI-generated images as sole original work.
